title: Flame Extinguishment Experiment (FLEX)
objective: Study heptane and methanol droplets in O2/N2 mixtures diluted with a second inert gas (nitrogen, carbon dioxide, helium or xenon) to see how an inert suppressant changes the flammability limit of the two fuels.
what_varied: Ambient O2, inert diluent type and amount, pressure, droplet size.
key_result: The flammability limit is lower in reduced gravity; the limiting oxygen index (LOI) is significantly lower than in normal gravity and lower than predicted. Stable cool flames form after radiative extinction of heptane droplets.
fire_safety_implication: Terrestrial standards for inert-gas suppressants do not offer the same margin of safety in low gravity as in normal gravity.
citation: NASA ISS Researcher's Guide: Combustion Science (NP-2015-10-034-JSC); PSI-69 (DOI 10.60555/mbq8-0451), p. 12-13, 33-34, 36, 52

title: Burning and Suppression of Solids (BASS)
objective: Examine burning and extinction of a wide variety of solid fuel samples in microgravity, to improve 1-g material fire-safety tests and guide extinguishing strategies.
what_varied: Airflow speed (main variable), oxygen (nitrogen dilution), nitrogen suppressant jet.
key_result: NASA-STD-6001 Test 1 is not conservative: materials can burn at lower oxygen in microgravity than on Earth. Local suppressant application was not adequate; the jet entrained air and sustained the flame, and nitrogen could even strengthen it.
fire_safety_implication: Materials screened as safe in 1-g may burn in a spacecraft; extinguisher placement needs rethinking because a suppressant jet can feed a microgravity flame.
citation: NASA ISS Researcher's Guide: Combustion Science (NP-2015-10-034-JSC); PSI-26 (sample list only), p. 18-22, 31, 45, 52

title: Water Mist Fire Suppression (Mist)
objective: Measure how water droplet diameter and water concentration affect the speed, strength and shape of premixed flames, to design better mist suppression systems replacing Halon.
what_varied: Water droplet diameter, water concentration, fuel and oxygen mixture.
key_result: Led to non-toxic water-mist portable fire extinguishers certified for spaceflight; the first two of nine reached the ISS in December 2015 to replace CO2 units.
fire_safety_implication: Direct path from microgravity research to a crew fire-suppression tool.
citation: NASA ISS Researcher's Guide: Combustion Science (NP-2015-10-034-JSC), p. 26

title: Smoke Aerosol Measurement Experiment (SAME)
objective: Measure the particle-size distribution of smoke from spacecraft materials.
what_varied: Spacecraft material.
key_result: Microgravity flames produce very different particulate sizes, so detectors that sense particulates need different signatures in space.
fire_safety_implication: Guidance for designers of future spacecraft smoke detectors.
citation: NASA ISS Researcher's Guide: Combustion Science (NP-2015-10-034-JSC), p. 26, 35, 45

title: Candle Flames (Mir)
objective: Observe a candle flame in long-duration microgravity aboard Mir.
what_varied: Not stated in the available sources.
key_result: Microgravity candle flames burned over 45 minutes, to a lower ambient oxygen than an identical candle on Earth, and oscillated before extinction.
fire_safety_implication: Refutes the belief that a steady fire cannot exist in quiescent microgravity.
citation: NASA ISS Researcher's Guide: Combustion Science (NP-2015-10-034-JSC); Dietrich et al. (2000), p. 9, 30, 33

title: Cool Flames (CIR initiative)
objective: Find the pre-conditions for hot-flame/cool-flame transitions, cool-flame stability and spontaneous re-ignition, using existing FLEX-2 MDCA hardware.
what_varied: Fuel type, pressure, diluent concentration.
key_result: Builds on FLEX: after hot-flame extinction, heptane droplets kept burning with a low-temperature cool flame.
fire_safety_implication: Very weak, persistent flames invisible to the eye can spontaneously re-ignite long after the visible flame is gone.

title: High oxygen turns droplet burns into bursts
objective: Compare how FLEX droplet tests ended at high vs air-level oxygen.
what_varied: Ambient O2 (all fuels, diluents and pressures pooled).
key_result: At O2 >= 0.25, 24 of 30 tests ended in Disruption (80%); at O2 <= 0.21, 22 of 206 (10.7%).
fire_safety_implication: In an oxygen-enriched habitat a burning droplet is more likely to burst and scatter fuel than to burn out quietly. Cells are small and pressure coverage is uneven, so treat this as a strong signal, not a law.
citation: Fire-Margin analysis of PSI-69 FLEX table (DOI 10.60555/mbq8-0451)

title: Where Moon-base fire evidence exists, and where it does not
objective: Check whether real tests reach the 34% O2 / 8.2 psia (0.558 atm) habitat atmosphere.
what_varied: Fuel type; PSI public data vs verified literature.
key_result: In PSI's public data, solid materials stop at 22.2% O2. Only 3 solid samples (Saffire-VI, 2024) burned near Moon-base conditions (29%-31% O2, ~0.54 atm): not in PSI, one flight, no partial gravity. Gas flames (CFI-G) were tested at 33%-39% O2 / 0.50 atm; FLEX droplets reach 34% O2 but only at >= 0.69 atm, and at O2 >= 25% 80% of FLEX tests ended in Disruption.
fire_safety_implication: Cabin-material and droplet fire behaviour at the planned habitat atmosphere rests on one literature flight: the next experiments should target that corner, including partial gravity.
citation: Fire-Margin analysis of PSI-69 FLEX table (DOI 10.60555/mbq8-0451); PSI-25; PSI-159; Urban et al., Preliminary Results from the Saffire VI Experiment, ICES-2024-365; test matrix in NTRS 20240007488 presentation

title: The d-squared law only fits droplets that burn out
objective: Check burn time against the d-squared law t = d0^2 / K.
what_varied: Test outcome (Completion vs early end).
key_result: For Completion tests, d0^2/K tracks measured burn time (r = 0.92, n = 27); across all tests r = 0.16 because extinction or disruption ends the burn early.
fire_safety_implication: Use d0^2/K as an upper limit on burn time, never as a prediction for droplets that may extinguish or burst.
citation: Fire-Margin analysis of PSI-69 FLEX table (DOI 10.60555/mbq8-0451); models/metrics.json

title: Three misconceptions about spacecraft fire
objective: Misconceptions that shaped early spacecraft fire safety.
what_varied: Not stated in the available sources.
key_result: (1) A steady fire cannot exist in a quiescent microgravity environment. (2) A fire will self-extinguish if ventilation is shut off. (3) Because the reduced-gravity environment is inherently safer, terrestrial fire standards and tests represent a very conservative approach to fire safety.
fire_safety_implication: Research at NASA GRC and in microgravity showed all three are false.
citation: NASA ISS Researcher's Guide: Combustion Science (NP-2015-10-034-JSC), p. 35

title: BASS-II: lower-oxygen burning in micro-g
key_result: Materials burn at lower oxygen concentrations in microgravity than in normal gravity.
fire_safety_implication: Shutting down ventilation may not extinguish flames in high-oxygen, low-pressure exploration atmospheres.
